title: Mix-ups
oneLiner: The services the exam puts side by side. Each group has one rule to tell them apart, a table of when each one isn't the answer, and a quiz that mixes them all.

notes.html: One rule: GuardDuty spots threats, Inspector spots vulnerabilities, Macie spots sensitive data, Security Hub collects them all.

head: Service
It answers
Not this when
rows: Threats from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs: crypto-mining, odd API calls, known bad IPs
You want to scan software for CVEs (Inspector)
Vulnerabilities (CVEs) and network exposure on EC2, ECR images, Lambda
You want to detect an attack in progress (GuardDuty)
Data lives in RDS or EBS
One place for findings from all of the above, plus best-practice standards (CIS, AWS FSBP)
You need the detection itself; it aggregates
Investigate a finding's root cause with a graph of activity
You need detection; it's for after a finding
Is a resource configured to my rules, and how did it change?
You need who made the call (CloudTrail)
Who called which API, when, from where
You need resource compliance over time (Config)

notes.html: One rule: Secrets Manager if it must rotate, Parameter Store if it's config, KMS for keys, CloudHSM only when you must own the HSM, ACM for TLS.

head: Service
It answers
Not this when
rows: Passwords and API keys with built-in rotation (RDS native), cross-region replicas
Plain config values; it costs per secret
Config and secrets in a hierarchy; standard tier is free
Encryption keys used by AWS services, envelope encryption, key policies
You need a single-tenant HSM under your sole control
Dedicated HSM you manage; custom crypto, Oracle TDE
Free public TLS certificates, auto-renewal, on ALB/CloudFront/API Gateway
TLS directly on EC2: the classic answer is that you can't install them there (exportable public certs exist since 2025, for a fee)

notes.html: One rule: SQS buffers for one consumer, SNS fans out, EventBridge routes by content, Kinesis streams in order with replay, Firehose loads with no code.

head: Service
It answers
Not this when
rows: Decouple and buffer; consumers pull; each message processed once
Many consumers each need every message
Push one message to many subscribers (fan-out, often to SQS)
Messages must wait for a slow consumer
Route events by content to targets; SaaS sources; schedules
Real-time, ordered per shard, replay, many consumers
You just want data landed in S3 (Firehose)
Load streams into S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, Splunk; buffers; no code
Existing apps on AMQP, MQTT, JMS, STOMP

notes.html: One rule: name what you're moving: files online, files over time with on-prem access, files by truck, files over SFTP, databases, or whole servers.

head: Service
It answers
Not this when
rows: One-time or scheduled online copy of files (NFS, SMB, HDFS, S3, EFS, FSx)
On-prem apps need ongoing local access (Storage Gateway)
On-prem apps keep using files, volumes or tapes backed by AWS
Terabytes to petabytes offline; edge compute
The link can move it in days
Partners send files over SFTP/FTPS/FTP/AS2 into S3 or EFS
Databases (and S3 → Kinesis) with CDC, minimal downtime

notes.html: One rule: CloudFront caches HTTP at the edge; Global Accelerator gives two static anycast IPs and fast failover for any TCP/UDP; Route 53 picks by DNS.

head: Service
It answers
Not this when
rows: Cache static and dynamic HTTP(S) content close to users; WAF; signed URLs
2 static anycast IPs, AWS backbone, failover in seconds, TCP/UDP
You want content cached (it doesn't cache)
Send users to the best region by DNS
Failover must ignore client DNS caching (TTL)

notes.html: One rule: peering for a few VPCs, Transit Gateway for many, PrivateLink to expose one service, endpoints to reach AWS services privately, VPN fast, Direct Connect consistent.

head: Service
It answers
Not this when
rows: A few VPCs, no extra hop, cheap
Hub for many VPCs and on-prem; transitive routing
One service to many VPCs/accounts; overlapping CIDRs fine
S3 and DynamoDB from private subnets; free; route table entry
Any other service, or access from on-prem
Other AWS services (and S3) through an ENI; works from on-prem over DX/VPN
Lowest cost S3 access within the VPC (gateway is free)
Encrypted over the internet; up in minutes
Private, consistent link; weeks to set up
Needed this week, or encryption by default (add VPN or MACsec)

notes.html: One rule: Athena for ad-hoc SQL on S3, Redshift for a warehouse, EMR for Spark/Hadoop you tune, Glue for serverless ETL and the catalog, OpenSearch for search and logs.

head: Service
It answers
Not this when
rows: Serverless SQL on S3, pay per data scanned
Heavy repeated BI joins all day (Redshift)
Data warehouse; complex joins; BI; Spectrum queries S3 too
Occasional queries on S3 (Athena is cheaper)
Managed Spark, Hadoop, Hive, Presto clusters

notes.html: One rule: SCPs and permission boundaries only cap; IAM and resource policies grant; Identity Center is for your staff, Cognito for your app's users.

head: Service
It answers
Not this when
rows: Cap what accounts in an Organization can ever do
Cap what one user or role can get, e.g. for delegated admins
Let another account or service reach a resource (S3, KMS, SQS)
Granting to your own users broadly (identity policy)
Workforce SSO into many accounts and apps
Sign-up and sign-in for app users; JWTs
Swap a login for temporary AWS credentials (e.g. upload to S3)
Just authenticating to your API (user pool)

items: "prevent any account from leaving a region"
"let developers create roles but not exceed X"
"employees sign in once to all accounts"

notes.html: One rule: Lambda for short events, Fargate for containers that run longer, App Runner for a web app with the least setup, Batch for queued jobs, Step Functions to chain the steps.

head: Service
It answers
Not this when
rows: Simplest possible web app deploy (App Runner)
Web app or API from source or image, with TLS and scaling built in
Queued batch jobs on EC2, Spot or Fargate
Orchestrate steps with retries, branching, waits, human approval

items: "deploy a container web app, least ops"

questions.q: An EC2 instance is suspected of crypto-mining and calling known malicious IPs. Which service detects this with the least setup?

options.why: Threat detection from flow logs, DNS and CloudTrail; one click to enable.

questions.q: Security must continuously scan EC2 instances and container images in ECR for known CVEs.

options.why: Vulnerability scanning for EC2, ECR and Lambda.
Shows findings from scanners; it doesn't scan itself.

questions.q: A company must find buckets that contain credit card numbers and passport data.

options.why: Detects suspicious access, not data contents.

questions.q: Findings from GuardDuty, Inspector and Macie across 40 accounts must appear in one place with compliance scores.

options.t: Security Hub with a delegated administrator
options.why: Aggregates findings and runs standards across the Organization.
Investigation graphs, not an aggregated dashboard.
Config compliance only, not GuardDuty or Macie findings.

questions.q: Database passwords must rotate every 30 days automatically with the least custom code.

options.why: No built-in rotation; you'd write a Lambda.
Rotates the key, not the password.

options.t: Store in S3 with a lifecycle rule

questions.q: An app needs feature flags and endpoint URLs per environment, at the lowest cost. Nothing needs rotation.

options.why: Billed per secret; rotation isn't needed.
Works, but more to build than Parameter Store.

questions.q: Regulations require encryption keys in a single-tenant HSM that only the company controls.

options.why: Dedicated HSM; AWS can't access the keys.

questions.q: One order event must reach a billing service, a shipping service and an analytics queue, each getting every message, and survive slow consumers.

options.t: SNS topic fanning out to an SQS queue per service
options.why: Fan-out plus a buffer for each consumer.

options.t: One SQS queue shared by all three
options.why: Each message would go to only one consumer.

options.t: Direct HTTP calls from the order service

questions.q: Clickstream events must be processed in real time, in order per user, by several consumers, with replay of the last 7 days.

options.why: Ordered per shard, many consumers, retention up to 365 days.
No ordering guarantee and no replay.
Loads to destinations; no replay to consumers.

questions.q: IoT data must land in S3 as Parquet every few minutes with no code and no servers.

options.why: Buffers, converts and delivers with no code.

options.t: Kinesis Data Streams with a custom consumer

questions.q: An on-prem app uses JMS and AMQP and must move to AWS with no code changes to messaging.

options.why: Managed ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ that speaks those protocols.

questions.q: A company wants to migrate 50 TB from NFS to EFS over its 10 Gbps link, then stop using the on-prem server.

options.why: Online, one-time or scheduled transfer with verification.
For ongoing on-prem access, not a one-off move.
The link can move 50 TB in about a day.

questions.q: A UDP game runs in two regions. Players need fixed IPs and failover in seconds when a region fails.

options.why: Static anycast IPs, TCP/UDP, fast health-based failover.

questions.q: A global news site serves the same images and pages to millions of readers and wants lower latency and origin load.

options.t: More EC2 instances in one region

questions.q: 120 VPCs across accounts and two data centers need to reach each other with the least operational overhead.
A SaaS provider must expose one API to hundreds of customer VPCs, many with overlapping CIDRs, without exposing the rest of its network.

options.why: Service-level access; overlapping CIDRs don't matter.
Overlapping CIDRs can't peer, and it exposes networks.
Routing between networks; CIDRs must not overlap.

questions.q: Analysts run occasional SQL queries on logs in S3 and want no infrastructure and to pay only when they query.

options.why: Serverless SQL on S3, billed per data scanned.
Running all the time for occasional queries.

questions.q: Developers may create IAM roles for their apps, but those roles must never get more than a set of allowed permissions.

options.t: Require a permission boundary on any role they create
An SCP on the developers' account
options.why: Caps the whole account, including admins.

options.t: A resource policy on each bucket

questions.q: A mobile app's signed-in users must upload photos directly to S3 with temporary AWS credentials.

options.t: Cognito identity pool, after sign-in with a user pool
options.why: Exchanges the login for scoped temporary credentials.
Gives tokens for your API, not AWS credentials.

options.t: An IAM user per app user

questions.q: An order workflow calls 5 Lambda functions in order, with retries, a branch on payment result, and a wait for manual approval.

options.why: Orchestrates steps, retries, branching and waits.

options.t: Chain Lambdas by having each call the next
options.why: Hard to retry and observe; and no long waits.
